title: Generalized Fallback Installers — ecosystem routes when no native package manager covers the OS
scope: Declarative `fallback: { go|npm|cargo|pip: "<first-party pkg>" }` slot on define_tool!. Platform slots always win; on is_no_platform_installer() the runtime tries fallback routes in declared order using the first toolchain on PATH, maps concrete version pins to ecosystem syntax, and runs package strings through validate_package_name. Install receipts (~/.jarvy/install-receipts.json) route fallback-installed tools to the right check-updates probe instead of the unchecked bucket. tool.installed gains install_route; tool.unsupported fires only when fallbacks are also unusable. betterleaks is the first consumer (deletes its bespoke custom_install, 4cadf92); ~20 'no first-party winget manifest' tools are migration candidates. Full PRD: tasks/prd-060-fallback-installers.md
follow_up: Phase 1: FallbackRoute type + macro slot + go/npm/cargo/pip runtime + validation + telemetry + betterleaks migration
Phase 2: install receipts + check-updates receipt routing + candidate-tool audit/migration (verify first-party packages per the verification rule)
Open: jarvy upgrade receipt-awareness in v1?
Open: pip vs pipx (PEP-668 externally-managed environments)
